taskDescription: Drag each term into the correct blank to complete the key facts of cholesterol synthesis and its regulation.
textField: The rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis is HMG-CoA *reductase*, which converts HMG-CoA to *mevalonate* using two NADPH. Cholesterol synthesis uses a *cytosolic* HMG-CoA synthase, whereas ketogenesis uses a *mitochondrial* one. *Statins* lower blood LDL by competitively inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase.

overallFeedback.feedback: HMG-CoA reductase is the committed step of cholesterol synthesis (cytosolic/ER pathway) — distinct from the mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase of ketogenesis. Its product mevalonate feeds the isoprenoid pathway to cholesterol. Statins exploit this by competitively inhibiting the reductase, which triggers SREBP-2-mediated up-regulation of LDL receptors and thereby lowers circulating LDL.
